description: Reconciles the source identifiers used by requirements.csv with the identifiers in the source register.
why_this_exists: requirements.csv was authored against an earlier source-identifier scheme
(SRC-EU-GDPR-001) which the register later replaced with descriptive ids
(SRC-GDPR-EURLEX). The two were never reconciled, so every one of the 11
source ids in the CSV was dangling: the rows looked cited, and none of the
citations resolved. Nothing failed, because nothing checked.
The mapping is recorded here as data rather than inside a script so that the
resolution of each identifier is reviewable by someone checking the law, and
so an unresolved one is visible instead of being quietly dropped.

resolution_basis.exact: The CSV id and the registered id name the same instrument; matched on the instrument, not on the id string.
resolution_basis.by_provision: Resolved using the row's own `source_provision` value, which names the instrument explicitly.
resolution_basis.assumed_current: Two registered versions exist and the row does not say which. Mapped to the version the register marks current, and listed under `requires_human_confirmation`.

SRC-US-STATE-MODEL-001.note: Generic state model. Not an authority; requirements resting on it are marked authority_level 'derived'.

SRC-CA-CCPA-001.note: CCPA/CPRA statutory text as published by the CPPA.

SRC-BR-LGPD-003.note: Row names 'Resolution CD/ANPD n 19/2024', which is the registered international-transfer resolution.

SRC-BR-LGPD-004.note: Row names 'Resolution CD/ANPD n 4/2023', which is the registered sanctions resolution.

SRC-CA-CCPA-004.note: Row names the 2025 CPPA amendments and concerns automated decision-making technology, which the register records as introduced by the regulations effective 2026-01-01.

SRC-CA-CCPA-003.note: Row cites only 'CCPA Regulations'. Both the 2023 and the 2026 regulations are registered, and the register marks 2023 historical and 2026 current. Mapped to current; the underlying rows (universal opt-out, retention) exist in both versions, so the choice affects which version the citation points at rather than whether the requirement exists.
